Definition: from G1508 and the neuter of G5100; if not somewhat:--except.
BiblicalUsage: This phrase means except or if not somewhat, and in the Greek text it stands as if followed by a single particle that asks whether, written as one word. The disciples say they have no more than five loaves and two fishes except they go and buy food, and Paul says husbands and wives should not deprive one another except by consent for a time. The phrase draws the one exception and holds everything else firm.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the exceptions in God's word are as careful as His commands, because He draws the line exactly where He means it.
